title: Cash Management and Financial Performance of Restaurant MSMEs: Evidence from an Emerging African Market
content: Cash management is vital to the survival of small restaurant businesses, yet evidence from African markets remains limited. This study examined how far restaurant micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Angola implement cash management strategies. It also assessed their financial performance and the relationship between the two. A descriptive-correlational design was used, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire from owners and managers of registered restaurants. Cash management strategies were highly implemented overall. Inventory control, planning and budgeting, and disbursement management were the strongest practices. The promotion of digital payments and the diversification of assets were the weakest. Respondents rated financial performance as excellent across liquidity, activity and profitability measures, although emergency liquidity was the least favourable area. A moderate, positive and significant relationship was found between cash management and financial performance. The findings suggest that restaurant MSMEs manage routine cash flows well but remain vulnerable to sudden shocks. Owners should strengthen contingency planning, build adequate reserves and actively promote digital payment channels. Support agencies and lenders can assist through targeted financial training. The study adds evidence from an under-researched sector in an emerging African market.
